predict.title: A constraint that doesn't match
options: The page throws: `abc` can't be converted to `int`
predict.explanation: `{Id:int}` is a **route constraint**. `abc` is not an integer, so this route **doesn't match at all**, and the router finds no other page. The user gets the not-found page (the Router's `NotFoundPage` in .NET 10). The page is never created, so there is no conversion error.

predict.title: Same page, new id
options: An error, because the same page can't be opened twice
predict.explanation: Going from `/products/1` to `/products/2` keeps the **same component instance**. Blazor only sets `Id` again, so `@Id` shows **2**. But `OnInitialized` runs **once per instance**, so `title` still says **Product 1**. Compute it in **`OnParametersSet`**, which runs on every parameter change.

predict.title: The Home link that is always active
predict.body:
NavMenu.razor:

```razor
<NavLink href="">Home</NavLink>
<NavLink href="orders">Orders</NavLink>
<NavLink href="admin">Admin</NavLink>
```

The app runs at the root of the site. The user is on `/orders/7`.

**Which links get the `active` class?**
options: None of them: `/orders/7` is not exactly `orders`
predict.explanation: The default match is **`NavLinkMatch.Prefix`**: a link is active when the URL **starts with** its path. `orders` is a prefix of `orders/7`, so **Orders** is active. The empty `href` of **Home** is a prefix of **every** URL, so Home is always active too. Add `Match="NavLinkMatch.All"` to the Home link.

predict.title: Which query value?
options: An error: the query has a `page` value that no property uses
predict.explanation: `Q` has no `Name`, so it reads the query value **`q`** (names ignore case): **cats**. `Page` has `Name = "p"`, so it reads **`p`**, not `page`. There is no `p` in the URL, so `Page` is `null` and the page shows **1**. Extra query values are simply ignored.

practice.title: Two URLs for one page
practice.task: Make **`Products.razor`** a page that opens at **`/products`** and also at **`/catalog`**.
practice.hint: A component can have more than one `@page` line.

checks.label: A `@page "/products"` line
checks.hint: Add `@page "/products"` on its own line at the top.

practice.title: Read a route parameter
practice.task:
Change **`ProductDetails.razor`** so it opens at URLs like **`/products/42`**: 1. The route has a parameter **`Id`** that only matches integers. 2. Add the matching **`int`** parameter property. 3. Render it as `

Product @Id

`.
practice.hint: Write the parameter in braces with a constraint: `{Id:int}`. The property needs `[Parameter]`.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public int Id` property
checks.hint: Inside `@code`, add `[Parameter] public int Id { get; set; }`.

practice.title: An optional parameter
practice.task:
**`Orders.razor`** should open at **`/orders`** (all orders) and at **`/orders/open`**, **`/orders/shipped`**, and so on. 1. Use **one** `@page` line with an **optional** parameter called **`Status`**. 2. Add a nullable `string` parameter property for it. 3. Show `

Orders: @(Status ?? "all")

`.
practice.hint: A `?` after the name makes a route parameter optional: `{Status?}`. When it's missing, the property is `null`.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public string? Status` property
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public string? Status { get; set; }`. It must be nullable, because `/orders` has no status.

checks.label: Shows `Status`, or `"all"` when it is null
Only one `@page` line
checks.hint: Use a single `@page` line with the optional parameter.

practice.title: Fix the page that doesn't update
practice.task:
The user opens `/products/1`, clicks **Next**, and the URL changes to `/products/2`, but the product name doesn't change.

Fix it: load the product in the lifecycle method that runs **every time the parameters are set**, not only once.
practice.hint: Blazor keeps the same component instance when only the route parameter changes. `OnInitializedAsync` runs once per instance (Level 4).

checks.label: The product is no longer loaded in `OnInitializedAsync`
checks.hint: Move the loading out of `OnInitializedAsync` (you can rename the method).

practice.title: Search with the query string
practice.task:
**`Search.razor`** opens at URLs like `/search?q=blazor&page=2`.

1. Fill **`Q`** from the query value `q`, and **`Page`** from the query value **`page`**.
2. The **Next page** button goes to the current URL with `page` set to the next number. Build the URL with **`GetUriWithQueryParameter`**, and navigate **without** a full page reload.
practice.hint: `[SupplyParameterFromQuery]` reads a query value. `GetUriWithQueryParameter` only **returns** a URL; pass it to `NavigateTo`.

checks.label: `Page` reads the query value `page` and is nullable
No full page reload (`forceLoad: true`)
checks.hint: Remove `forceLoad: true`: a link inside the app doesn't need a reload.

practice.title: A nav menu, from scratch
practice.task:
Write **`NavMenu.razor`** with, inside `<nav>`:

- A **Home** `NavLink` to `""` that is active **only** on the home page.
- An **Orders** `NavLink` to `"orders"` that is also active on `/orders/7` and other sub-pages.
- An **Admin** `NavLink` to `"admin"` that uses the CSS class **`selected`** instead of `active`.
- A **Log out** button that goes to `"logout"` with a **full page reload** (it's a server endpoint, not a Blazor page).
practice.hint: Home needs `Match="NavLinkMatch.All"`. The default match (`Prefix`) is right for Orders. `ActiveClass` changes the class name. Inject `NavigationManager` for the button.

checks.label: Orders keeps the default prefix match (no `NavLinkMatch.All`)
checks.hint: Remove `Match="NavLinkMatch.All"` from Orders, or it won't be active on `/orders/7`.

checks.label: Injects `NavigationManager`
checks.hint: Add `@inject NavigationManager Navigation` at the top.

checks.label: Log out calls `NavigateTo("logout", forceLoad: true)`
checks.hint: In the click handler, call `Navigation.NavigateTo("logout", forceLoad: true);`.

options: A build error: only one `@page` is allowed
Only the last one, `/catalog`, is used
quiz.explanation: A component can have **several `@page` directives**. Each one adds a route to the same component. There is no redirect: the URL stays as the user typed it.

quiz.body: A page has `[Parameter] public int Id { get; set; }`. Which route makes `/products/42` work and `/products/abc` **not** match?
quiz.explanation: The syntax is **`{name:constraint}`**, and the integer constraint is **`int`**. There is no `number` constraint. Without a constraint, the route matches any text, and a non-number fails when Blazor converts it to `int`.

quiz.body: A page has `@page "/files/{*Path}"` and `[Parameter] public string? Path { get; set; }`. The user opens `/files/docs/2026/a.pdf`. What is `Path`?
options: `null`: the URL has too many segments
quiz.explanation: `{*Path}` is a **catch-all** parameter: it takes **the rest of the URL**, slashes included. It must be the last segment of the route and its property must be a `string`.

quiz.body: When should you call `Navigation.NavigateTo(url, forceLoad: true)`?
options: Every time, so the page always has fresh data
When the target page has route parameters
When the URL is not a Blazor page, like a server endpoint (`/logout`) or a file download
When you want the **Back** button to skip the current page
quiz.explanation: `forceLoad: true` makes the browser do a **full page load** from the server, so the Blazor app starts again. Use it only to leave the router: server endpoints, downloads, other sites. Skipping the history entry is `replace: true`.

quiz.body: The current URL is `/search?q=cats&page=1`. What does `Navigation.GetUriWithQueryParameter("page", 2)` do?
options: It returns `/search?page=2` (the other query values are removed)
It **returns** the full URL with `page=2` and `q=cats` kept, without navigating
It changes the `Page` property of the current page to `2`
quiz.explanation: `GetUriWithQueryParameter` only **builds a string**: the current URL with that query value added or replaced, the others kept. To go there, pass it to `NavigateTo`. Passing `null` as the value removes the parameter.

quiz.body: A menu has `<NavLink href="orders">Orders</NavLink>`. The user is on `/orders/7/edit`. Does the link get the `active` class?
options: Yes: the default match is `Prefix`, and the URL starts with `orders`
No: the default match is `All`, so only `/orders` matches
No: `NavLink` only checks the first segment of the URL when `Match` is set
quiz.explanation: **`NavLinkMatch.Prefix`** is the default: the link is active when the current URL **starts with** its path. Use `Match="NavLinkMatch.All"` when only an exact match should count, which is what the Home link needs.

quiz.body: The app's base URL is `https://site.com/app/`. The current URL is `https://site.com/app/orders/7?x=1`. What does `Navigation.ToBaseRelativePath(Navigation.Uri)` return?
quiz.explanation: `ToBaseRelativePath` removes **`BaseUri`** from the start of the URL. `BaseUri` always ends in `/`, so the result has no leading slash, and the query string is kept.

quiz.body: You want `/archive` and `/archive/2` to open the same page, with the page number as an `int`. Which is right?
quiz.explanation: An optional parameter ends with **`?`**, after the constraint: `{Page:int?}`. Use a **nullable** property (`int?`) so `/archive` gives `null`. Without `?`, `/archive` doesn't match.

quiz.body: After a payment, the code calls `Navigation.NavigateTo("checkout/done", replace: true)`. What does `replace: true` change?
options: The current history entry is replaced, so **Back** doesn't return to the payment page
The page reloads from the server
The `checkout/done` component is created again even if it already exists
The current page's parameters are replaced, without changing the URL
quiz.explanation: `replace: true` **replaces** the current entry in the browser history instead of adding a new one. The user can't go **Back** to the payment form. It still navigates inside the app, with no reload.

quiz.body: In a .NET 10 app, `/products/999` matches the route `{Id:int}`, but product 999 doesn't exist in the database. How can the page show the app's not-found page?
quiz.explanation: In .NET 10, **`NavigationManager.NotFound()`** tells Blazor to show the not-found page (the Router's `NotFoundPage`) for the current URL, and sets a 404 status during static server rendering. Navigating to a `404` URL changes the address and does not send a 404 status.

interview.question: How does routing work in Blazor?
interview.modelAnswer: A component becomes a page with `@page "/route"`. The `Router` in `Routes.razor` scans the app's assembly for these routes, matches the current URL, and renders the page with `RouteView` inside its layout. Navigation between pages happens in the browser without a full reload.

interview.question: How do you get a value from the URL path into a page?
interview.modelAnswer: With a route parameter: put a name in braces in the route, like `@page "/products/{Id:int}"`, and add a `[Parameter]` property with the same name (case doesn't matter). A constraint like `:int` checks the type; if the URL breaks it, the route doesn't match.

interview.question: What happens when no route matches the URL?
interview.modelAnswer: The router shows the not-found content. In .NET 10 it's the component set in the Router's `NotFoundPage` parameter; older apps use a `<NotFound>` block. A page can also call `NavigationManager.NotFound()` when, for example, the item in the URL doesn't exist.

interview.question: How do you read the query string in a Blazor page?
interview.modelAnswer: Add `[SupplyParameterFromQuery]` to a property of the page. It reads the query value with the same name, or the one given with `Name = "..."`. Use nullable types so a missing value is `null`. To build a URL with a changed value, use `GetUriWithQueryParameter`.

interview.question: What is `NavigationManager` used for?
interview.modelAnswer: It reads the current URL (`Uri`, `BaseUri`, `ToBaseRelativePath`) and navigates from code with `NavigateTo`. `forceLoad: true` does a full page load from the server, for non-Blazor URLs; `replace: true` replaces the history entry. It also has the `LocationChanged` event.

interview.question: What is `NavLink`, and what does `NavLinkMatch` control?
interview.modelAnswer: `NavLink` renders an `<a>` that adds a CSS class (`active` by default, or `ActiveClass`) when its URL is the current one. `NavLinkMatch.Prefix`, the default, matches when the URL starts with the link's path; `NavLinkMatch.All` needs the whole URL to match, which is what a Home link needs.

interview.question: A page loads a product by route id. Going from `/products/1` to `/products/2` keeps showing product 1. Why, and how do you fix it?
interview.modelAnswer: Blazor reuses the same component instance and only sets the parameters again, so `OnInitializedAsync` doesn't run a second time. Load the data in `OnParametersSetAsync`, which runs every time the parameters are set.

interview.question: What are optional and catch-all route parameters?
interview.modelAnswer: An optional parameter ends with `?`, like `{Status?}` or `{Page:int?}`, so the URL works with or without it, and the property is `null` when it's missing. A catch-all, `{*Path}`, takes the rest of the URL including slashes into a `string`. Both must be the last segment.
